title: What dot picture explains the up and down sums?
description: A square grid of dots, four rows of four, is tilted into a diamond, and its slanting rows are counted from top to bottom. The counts climb to four and fall back, matching the up and down sum. This is the picture the book asks for.
teaching_notes: One idea: tilt a square grid and count its slanting rows to see the up and down sum. Watch for students who count only half of the diamond.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (Try This), p.8
video_script.why: The child draws a picture that explains why up and down sums of counting numbers are square numbers, using the method of the book's solved example.
video_script.substitution: A four by four grid of dots is used instead of the three by three grid of the solved example.
video_script.anchor: a square grid of dots tilted into a diamond
video_script.payoff_line: A diamond of dots with rows that climb and fall is a tilted square grid

final_answer.value: a diamond of dots with rows 1, 2, 3 up to n and back down, giving n x n dots
final_answer.spoken: a tilted square grid of dots

maths_rules: 4 x 4 = 16 dots in a grid of 4 rows of 4
tilted 4 by 4 grid has slanting rows of 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1 dots
an n by n grid tilted has rows 1, 2, ..., n, ..., 2, 1 and n x n dots
video_script.design: Same picture as the solved example, one size bigger. The grid is drawn, tilted, counted along its rows and checked against the sum.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about adding counting numbers up and then down.
<bookmark mark='sums'/>Sums like one plus two plus one give square numbers.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book asks for a picture that explains why. What picture of dots could do that?

beats.on_screen: the sums stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: an empty square grid frame with dot positions; a tilted copy beside it

marks.way: the sums move to the side
marks.grid: an empty square grid frame appears, the same number of dots in every row

beats.removed: the empty picture frame is replaced by a grid frame
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>A square grid has the same number of dots in every row. The dots can be counted along slanting lines too.

marks.given: the up and down sums are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the counting numbers are added up and then down, giving one, four, nine and so on.

beats.on_screen: To find: a picture that shows why these sums are square numbers
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a picture that shows why these sums are square numbers.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: square grid, 4 rows of 4 dots = 4 x 4 dots

marks.draw: the square grid of four rows of four dots appears with 4 x 4 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='draw'/>Step one, draw a square grid of dots with four rows of four. That is four times four dots.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: tilt the grid so one corner faces up; it becomes a diamond of dots

marks.tilt: the grid turns until one corner faces up and becomes a diamond

beats.moves_through: the grid turns a quarter of a turn
narration: <bookmark mark='tilt'/>Step two, tilt the grid so that one corner faces up. It becomes a diamond of dots, with slanting rows.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: count each slanting row from the top: 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1 dots

marks.count: the rows are lit from top to bottom with the counts beside them
marks.climb: the counts are joined by arrows that go up to four and back down

beats.colours: each row in a different shade
narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step three, count the dots in each slanting row from the top.
<bookmark mark='climb'/>The rows have one, two, three, four, three, two and one dots. The counts climb to four and fall back.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 16 and 4 x 4 = 16, the same dots

marks.check: the sum of the row counts is written next to 4 x 4, and both show the same dots

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the picture against the sum. The row counts add up to sixteen, and four times four is also sixteen.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a diamond of dots with rows 1, 2, 3, ..., n, ..., 3, 2, 1 is an n by n grid, n x n dots

marks.ans: the answer is boxed beside the tilted grid
marks.any: a bigger tilted grid appears beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A diamond of dots with rows that climb and fall is a tilted square grid. <bookmark mark='any'/>This works for a grid of any size, so every up and down sum is a square number.
